neet_phy_u03_t07_1.working: Friction supplies the centripetal force: mv²/r = μmg, so v = √(μrg) = √(0.4×10×100) = √400 = 20 m/s.

neet_phy_u03_t07_2.working: No lateral thrust requires tanθ = v²/(rg) = 400/4000 = 0.1. For small θ, h ≈ d·tanθ = 1.5×0.1 = 0.15 m = 15 cm.

neet_phy_u03_t07_4.working: Optimum speed on a banked road is √(rg tanθ) (A-II). Maximum safe speed on a level road is √(μrg) (B-III). A cyclist's lean satisfies tanθ = v²/(rg) (C-IV). At the optimum speed, N cosθ = mg, so N = mg/cosθ (D-I).

neet_phy_u03_t07_5.working: A is false: below the optimum speed, friction acts up the slope. B is true: v = √(μrg) has no mass dependence. C is true: the vehicle stays at rest if μs ≥ tanθ. D is false: N = mg/cosθ. E is true: the outer rail is raised. So B, C and E are correct.
